review.note:
# SLICE-58 lite re-review of commit 3da30080

Scope: verify the three matcher fixes requested by review A and B (fence-char
tracking for ~~~ vs ``` without cross-closing, indented-code-block detection
with the same runner-prefix / plugin-root-wrap guard, bun.exe recognized as a
runner) in both twins, plus mirrored tests, test run, and lint.

## Findings

1. Twin identity: `diff src/scripts/lib/source-script-path-rule.mts
   crew/scripts/lib/source-script-path-rule.mts` shows the two files are
   identical except for the header comment block naming which copy is
   canonical vs duplicate. No logic drift between twins.
2. Fence tracking: `FENCE_RE` keys on fence char (`` ` `` or `~`), requires
   3+ repeats, allows up to 3 leading spaces (CommonMark). `fenceChar` state
   only closes on a matching character; a `~~~` inside an open ``` block
   is treated as ordinary content and does not close the fence (confirmed by
   both new tests "a stray ~~~ inside an open \`\`\` fence does not close it").
3. Indented-code branch (`INDENTED_CODE_RE`, 4+ spaces or tab) routes through
   `scanIndentedCodeLine`, which calls the same `matchedPathInInvocationForm`
   guard as the inline-code-span path — requires a runner prefix
   (`bun`/`bun.exe`/`node`/`bunx` + whitespace) or the
   `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/` wrap immediately before the path. `bun.exe` is
   now in `RUNNER_PREFIX_RE` (`bun(?:\.exe)?`).
4. False-positive check: because the indented branch reuses the same prefix
   guard, a 4-space-indented list continuation that only mentions a path in
   prose (no runner prefix) does not match — confirmed by inspection, no
   regression test needed since the guard is identical to the pre-existing
   inline-code-span logic already covered by prior tests.
5. Tests mirror 1:1 across `src/tests/validate-source-script-path-refs.test.mts`
   and `crew/tests/validate-agents-no-source-script-path.test.mts` (4 new
   cases each: ~~~ fence, stray ~~~ inside ``` fence, 4-space indented bare
   invocation, bun.exe invocation).

## Verification run

- `bun test src/tests/validate-source-script-path-refs.test.mts
  crew/tests/validate-agents-no-source-script-path.test.mts` → 21 pass, 0
  fail, 16 expect() calls.
- `bunx biome lint` on all four touched files (both directories, each with
  its own biome config) → clean, no fixes applied, no complexity warnings.

## Decision

approved_with_notes is not needed — all requested fixes are present, correct,
tested, and green. Decision: **approved**.

review.note:
SLICE-56 review B (correctness), commits 461bf617 + 5b186335 on ee8735a1.

Verification performed independently (not trusting builder counts):
- Baseline grep for crew/scripts/crew.mts|src/scripts/loop.mts|report-to-pr.mts|prune-artifacts.mts|watch-tick.mts in agents/ (excl. 3rdparty): 53 hits across 19 files at ee8735a1, 0 at HEAD. agents/3rdparty/ untouched (empty diff --stat).
- Read full agents/ diff line by line: every changed line swaps only the script-path token (crew/scripts/crew.mts -> "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/dist/crew.js", src/scripts/loop.mts -> ".../dist/loop.js"); all flags/quoting/args byte-identical otherwise.
- Scope: git diff --stat ee8735a1..HEAD touches only the 19 agents/*.md files, the consumer-smoke test, and crew artifacts/slice file. No commands/, skills/, templates/, docs/, CLAUDE.md, dist/, src/scripts/.
- Ran src/tests/install/consumer-smoke.test.mts: 4 pass / 1 fail. EXPECTED_FAIL === ["dist/loop.js dispatch prepare"] exactly; newlyBroken=[] and nowPassing=[] both held (no assertion failure on those lines); failure is only the designed-red "stay red while EXPECTED_FAIL non-empty" assertion.
- Reproduced independently from a clean temp dir with CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT set: both `dispatch prepare` and `dispatch finalize` crash identically with `error: Module not found ".../dist/dispatch.mts"` -- a genuine module-resolution error, not an argument error.
- Investigated why only `prepare` appears in EXPECTED_FAIL: read src/scripts/lib/install/shipped-entrypoints.mts. listMarkdownCliEntrypoints dedups by `${file}::${firstArg}`; for agents/swarm.md both dispatch call sites have firstArg "dispatch" (prepare/finalize is args[1]), so the scanner silently drops the second occurrence (finalize) and only ever registers/runs "dispatch prepare". This dedup logic is pre-existing and untouched by this diff -- the slice's rewrite only made the quoted dist/loop.js dispatch line visible to CLI_LINE_RE for the first time (bare unquoted form was invisible before). The slice does not introduce or worsen any hiding of a crash; it is a pre-existing scanner blind spot that now also affects `finalize`, fully disclosed in the test's inline comment and in AC-1/AC-5 evidence and the builder handoff. Not a regression, but a real residual gap: `dispatch finalize`'s crash is currently untested and unratcheted.
- The "2 dependent assertion fixes" (bun count 30->29, and asserting crew/scripts/crew.mts is now ABSENT from grouped.bun) are necessary consequences of the drain: independently confirmed commands/ has no remaining literal quoted invocations of the old paths (only two unrelated prose mentions), so crew.mts correctly has zero remaining producers of a bun entry.
- Full suite: `bun test src/tests/ --parallel --timeout 60000` with the 6 agreed path-ignores: 3418 pass / 7 skip / 1 fail (the same designed-red consumer-smoke assertion). No other failures; did not need to rerun anything as a flake.
- Slice file (SLICE_56_REPOINT-...) and handoff: ACs ticked with concrete evidence (grep counts, test run numbers, exact crash signature), no placeholder/"bullet 1" text, no leaked FORBIDDEN/RETURN task-scoped markers. Handoff explicitly reports an unrelated stray environment reminder it encountered and correctly ignored (matches what this review also observed independently).

Decision: approved_with_notes.
Note for follow-up (not a blocker for this slice's stated scope): `dist/loop.js dispatch finalize` crashes with the same module-resolution error as `prepare` but is invisible to the ratchet due to the pre-existing file+firstArg dedup in listMarkdownCliEntrypoints. Recommend the dedup key include the full args (or at minimum firstArg+secondArg) so finalize gets its own label and EXPECTED_FAIL entry when the follow-up dist/dispatch.js fix lands -- otherwise a future fix to `prepare` alone could leave `finalize` silently broken forever.

review.note: Independent correctness review (ladder slot B) of SLICE-55 / FEAT-037 (commits 0e3b28ca, 4ee113fb) against commands/*.md repointed to dist/ bundles plus consumer-smoke ratchet classification. Verified independently: all 135 of 138 baseline source-path invocations in commands/ are rewritten to the correct dist/*.js form with no argument, flag, or quoting drift; the 3 remaining raw-pattern hits (orchestrate-slice.md:145-146, triage.md:60) are genuine historical/explanatory prose, not live invocations. agents/, skills/, templates/, CLAUDE.md marker blocks, docs/, and crew/scripts/validate-agents.mts are untouched, matching the slice's declared boundary. The commands/watch.md prose fix plus watch-scheduler-setup.test.mts AC-8 update are explicitly in-scope collateral (documented in the slice file) because the dist rewrite legitimately splits the previously-identical consumer command path from the scheduler's local-checkout path; confirmed the test now checks each path independently and still passes. Ran the consumer-smoke suite myself: exactly one assertion fails, the designed-red "EXPECTED_FAIL non-empty" check; newlyBroken=[] and nowPassing=[] both pass; EXPECTED_FAIL holds exactly the 6 agents-origin crew.mts labels, each independently confirmed via direct execution to crash with "Cannot find module '@astragenie/plugin-std'" (real module-resolution crashes, not mislabeled). The AC-2 floor assertions (CLI entries >=42, dist/hooks >=11) pass. Reviewed all 38 arg-error-classified entries' raw messages: every one is a genuine CLI argument/precondition error (missing config, invalid repo path placeholder, required flag, mkdir ENOENT from a literal "$PWD" token) with no module-resolution signature; spot-verified dist/watch-tick.js's truncated message directly and confirmed it is a real ENOENT on a missing registry file, not a disguised crash. The classifier's own unit tests directly prove a module-resolution crash lands in newlyBroken when absent from EXPECTED_FAIL, closing the "can the classifier hide a real crash" question without needing a synthetic fixture. Ran AC-5 manually from a clean directory: dist/crew.js audit exits 0 with real JSON; dist/loop.js status exits 1 with its own "No .claude/loop.json found" message, no module-resolution error -- both satisfy AC-5. Gates: validate-agent-refs, validate-content-length, validate-repo-boundary, validate-manifests, validate-dispatch-markers, build-dist --check, generate-metrics-band --check, typecheck, format:check all rc=0. bun test src/tests/ --parallel: pass count varies 3502-3505 across repeated runs with 1-5 failures beyond the designed-red consumer-smoke test; traced the extra failures to auto-merge.test.mts / synergy.test.mts / slice-complete-tracker-close.test.mts (none touched by this diff) and confirmed they pass 100% (3/3 runs, 36/36 tests) both on this branch and on the pre-slice baseline (719beda8) when run in isolation -- genuine pre-existing parallel-execution flakiness, not a regression, though the builder's self-report named the wrong flaky family ("slice-linker" instead of the auto-merge/synergy/tracker group actually observed). crew test suite: 1834 pass, 1 fail (validate-contracts redocly timeout) -- matches the builder's reported numbers exactly. Overall: implementation is accurate, complete, and within scope; the only issues found are non-blocking documentation/cosmetic nits.

validation.note:
FEAT-026/SLICE-52 ("Audit T2: self-contained dist bundles so hook entry
points run without node_modules") validated end to end at worktree HEAD
2041ce35 (full diff vs base 5fe21f91; fix delta b1dd6148..2041ce35).

All five acceptance criteria PASS. No regressions in either test suite
beyond the one designed-red ratchet assertion (DEC-044), which is present
identically on the main checkout (5cc59c58) and is explicitly scoped to
stay red until W2.5 clears the commands/*.md CLI path rewrite.

AC-1 (consumer-smoke / hook entries clean): PASS. `bun test
src/tests/install/consumer-smoke.test.mts` -> 2 pass, 1 fail. The one
failure is the designed-red "(c) Stay red while EXPECTED_FAIL is
non-empty" assertion in the ratchet test itself (DEC-044) -- not a hook
regression. `newlyBroken` and `nowPassing` both resolved to `[]`: no HOOK
entry is broken, and every entry still in EXPECTED_FAIL (all CLI-only,
`crew.mts`/`loop.mts`/`prune-artifacts.mts`/`watch-tick.mts`) is still
genuinely crashing without node_modules, as designed -- none belongs to
a hooks.json `bun` command.

AC-2 (dist/crew.js, dist/loop.js run without node_modules): PASS. Staged
a full node_modules-free copy of the worktree (everything except
node_modules/.git/.worktrees, mirroring stageConsumerCopy's own exclusion
rule) under a scratch temp dir, set CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT to that staged
root. `install-global`, `init --repo <tmp> --allow-existing`,
`cost-setup --repo <tmp>` against dist/crew.js and `list-presets`,
`install --repo <tmp2> --preset dotnet-python` against dist/loop.js all
returned rc 0 with real JSON output, no ENOENT. Caveat: a staging
attempt that copied ONLY dist/+templates/+hooks/hooks.json (not the full
tree) failed loop.js's preset commands with ENOENT scanning
`<root>/scripts/presets` -- `scripts/presets/*.json` is plain data that
ships as ordinary repo content (not bundled into dist/, not copied by
build-dist.mts), so a correct consumer-footprint staging must carry the
whole non-node_modules tree, matching exactly what
shipped-entrypoints.mts's own stageConsumerCopy does. Not a product bug,
a staging-scope correction.

With CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT unset (documented per instructions, not a PASS/
FAIL condition -- spec requires only the set case): `loop.js list-presets`
and `loop.js install --preset dotnet-python` both rc 1, ENOENT scanning a
nonsensical path three directories above the staged root
(`config-resolver.mts`'s unset-env fallback resolves relative to the
bundled dist/loop.js's own dirname, which under the single-file bundle
no longer sits at the pre-bundle depth assumed by that fallback chain).
This only matters if CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT is ever omitted in production,
which the hook/CLI contract does not do.

AC-3 (otel-post-tool-use.js, no @opentelemetry packages): PASS. Verified
zero `@opentelemetry` paths anywhere in the staged tree. With
CREW_OTEL_ENABLED=1, a consumer `.claude/crew/telemetry.yaml` containing
`enabled: true`, CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR and the payload's `cwd` both set to
the consumer directory as a native Windows backslash path, two separate
invocations of `bun dist/hooks/otel-post-tool-use.js` each returned rc 0
and each appended exactly one `otel_unavailable` line to
`.claude/logs/events.jsonl` (2 runs -> 2 lines total). The in-process
`warnedMissingDeps` one-shot guard is per-process, so "exactly one line"
holds per invocation as the AC requires; it does not dedupe across
separate hook invocations, which is expected (every hook call is a fresh
Bun process).

AC-4 (build:dist --check staleness + Bun-version pin): PASS. Clean tree:
`bun run build:dist -- --check` -> rc 0, "dist/ is up to date". A
behavioral (non-comment, non-dead-code) edit to `hooks/pre-push-gate.mts`
(added a branch to `isPushCommand`'s regex) -> rc 1, correctly naming
`hooks/pre-push-gate.js` as stale; reverted (`git checkout --`) -> rc 0
again. Note for future edits to this check: a comment-only addition and
an unused top-level `const` both did NOT trip staleness detection in two
earlier attempts -- Bun's bundler evidently drops both as part of normal
bundling even with `minify:false`, so `--check`'s byte-compare only
detects edits that change bundled, reachable code, consistent with the
AC's own wording ("non-comment edit"). Bun-version mismatch: temporarily
set `.bun-version` to `9.9.9` -> both `build:dist` and `build:dist
--check` rc 1 with a clear "Bun version mismatch" message naming pinned
vs running versions; reverted -> rc 0 again.

AC-5 (hooks.json / repo-boundary / metrics-band / gate-count agreement):
PASS. All 20 `bun` commands in `hooks/hooks.json` match
`bun "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/dist/hooks/<name>.js"` and every named file
exists under `dist/hooks/`. All 17 non-bun (`node`/`bash`) commands are
byte-identical to `git show 5fe21f91:hooks/hooks.json`.
`validate-repo-boundary.mts` -> rc 0; `--write-inventory` rewrote
`docs/planning/hooksjson-crew-path-inventory.json` with an empty `git
diff` afterward (byte-identical). `generate-metrics-band.mts --check` ->
rc 0. `docs/ci-gates.md` and `CLAUDE.md`'s `## CI gates` list both
enumerate exactly 43 contiguous gates (1-43), and gate 21 is
`build-dist.mts --check` in both.

Regression: `bun run typecheck` (3 tsc projects: root tsconfig.json,
tsconfig.test.json, crew/tsconfig.json) -> all rc 0, no errors. `bun test
src/tests/ --parallel --timeout 60000` -> 3502 pass, 7 skip, 1 fail
(3510 total, 344 files); the 1 failure is the same designed-red AC-1
ratchet assertion discussed above. Confirmed the identical single
failure (same assertion, same file) also occurs on the main checkout
(C:\work\mega\devcrew, read-only, HEAD 5cc59c58) when run standalone --
not a regression introduced by this slice. `cd crew && bun test
--timeout 60000 tests/ --parallel` -> 1793 pass, 117 skip, 0 fail (1910
total, 182 files) -- fully clean.
